title: Bolt-circle flange
prompt: Round flange for a 25 mm pipe: Ø80 mm, 8 mm thick, a Ø25 mm bore through the centre, and six M6 bolt holes (close fit) evenly spaced on a Ø62 mm bolt circle with the first one on +X. Put a 1 mm chamfer on the top outside edge. Centre it on the origin, standing on Z = 0, and make the number of bolt holes a parameter called bolts. Make the bolt holes hole features with the M6 preset.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
The bolt holes on a Ø62 circle, the first on +X
One Ø25 bore on the axis
One conical face: the top chamfer
The chamfer is on the top edge: it lowers the centroid to z = 3.9868 (on the bottom edge it would be 4.0132)
π·40²·8 − chamfer ring − bore − 6 bolt holes = 34617 mm³ ±0.1% (the chamfer removes 125 mm³)
bolts = 8 puts eight holes on the circle
bolts = 8 drills two more Ø6.4 holes: 34616.62 − 2·π·3.2²·8 = 34101.90 mm³ ±0.1%

notes: π·40²·8 = 40212.39; 1 mm chamfer ring 2π·(40 − 1/3)·0.5 = 124.62; bore π·12.5²·8 = 3926.99; M6 close fit Ø6.4: 6·π·3.2²·8 = 1544.17 → 34616.6 mm³. Construction: bolt_holes reads the hole features the prompt asks for (no geometry equivalent in the report), so a correct part built otherwise fails only that test (candidate --circle-cut-bolt-holes).
